exposure: Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25OHD) levels at birth (in infants and mothers)
Low 25OHD level (<=30 nmol/L) in preterm infants at birth
outcome: Duration of intermittent positive-pressure ventilation during resuscitation at delivery
cohort: The study included 94 preterm infants (<32 weeks gestation) and their mothers.
finding: A low serum 25OHD level (<=30 nmol/L) in preterm infants at birth was associated with increased oxygen requirement, increased duration of intermittent positive-pressure ventilation during resuscitation, and greater need for assisted ventilation, indicating an association with acute respiratory morbidity.
